rationale: Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS virtual-mailbox service, and such a service could plausibly publish llms.txt or agent-oriented docs, so the axis applies. A direct probe of https://www.anytimemailbox.com/llms.txt returned HTTP 404. None of the documentation evidence mentions agent-oriented, machine-readable, or LLM-targeted docs; it covers only consumer and mail-center product pages and help articles.

A virtual mailbox SaaS could plausibly offer AI insights, such as mail summaries, categorization or action suggestions, so the axis applies. The evidence pack only documents manual mail handling: scanning, forwarding, shredding, check deposit, storage and multi-user access. There is no evidence of any AI-generated insights or suggestions inside the product.

Background automation, such as auto-scan or auto-forward rules, is a plausible capability for a virtual mailbox service, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes manually requested, operator-performed actions (scan, forward, shred "with a few taps") and scheduled pickups. Nothing documents autonomous rules or triggers, and probes found no llms.txt or OpenAPI spec.

A built-in AI assistant is a plausible feature for a virtual-mailbox SaaS, so the axis applies. The evidence pack never mentions any AI assistant. The only delegation it documents is asking human mail-center operators to scan, forward or shred mail, which is a different capability and earns no credit.

Headless or programmatic automation is a fair question for a SaaS mailbox service, since such a service could expose an API or CLI, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes management through a phone app, web portal, or "few taps" in the UI. Probes found no OpenAPI spec and no llms.txt, and nothing documents an API, CLI, or headless/CI mode.

Anytime Mailbox is a virtual mailbox and mail-center SaaS. Its documented features cover mail scanning, forwarding, shredding, check deposit and street addresses, and nothing in the evidence shows an AI agent or assistant that could consume tools from MCP servers. Acting as an MCP client is a category error for this type of product, so the axis does not apply.

Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS virtual mailbox platform for which an official MCP server is a plausible offering, but no evidence shows one exists. The docs only describe web and mobile app mail management, and the probes found no llms.txt or OpenAPI spec.

Operating a virtual-mailbox SaaS through natural-language commands is a fair question, since such a service could ship an AI assistant or chat interface, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes tap- and click-based management through a phone app or web portal (scan, forward, shred, schedule pickup), with no natural-language or conversational interface. The probes found no llms.txt and no OpenAPI spec.

Anytime Mailbox is a virtual mailbox SaaS, and a service like this could plausibly ship an official CLI, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes a phone app, a web portal and an operator cloud dashboard, with nothing about any command-line tool. Probes also found no llms.txt or OpenAPI spec that would point to programmatic tooling.

A public API is a fair question for a SaaS virtual-mailbox service, so the axis applies. However, the evidence only describes management through the phone app, web portal and operator cloud login (docs-27, docs-43). Probes found no OpenAPI spec and no llms.txt at any candidate path, so there is no evidence of a documented public API.

Anytime Mailbox is a virtual-mailbox SaaS, so scoped API credentials for an agent are a fair capability to ask about, and the axis applies. The pack documents no API, API keys or scoped tokens; probes for OpenAPI and llms.txt all returned 404. Sharing access with multiple team users is a related human-account feature, not least-privilege programmatic credentials, so it earns no credit.

Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS virtual-mailbox platform, so official SDKs are a fair question, but the evidence pack never mentions an SDK, API, or developer library. Probes for an OpenAPI spec and llms.txt all returned 404. Every documented capability is end-user access through the web portal and mobile app.

Webhooks for events such as new mail arrival are a fair question for a virtual-mailbox SaaS platform, so the axis applies. The evidence pack documents no registrable outbound HTTP callbacks. The only mentions of remote management are app and web-portal access, and probes found no public API or OpenAPI spec.

Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS platform that could plausibly publish an API, so the axis applies. However, the evidence documents only a phone app and web portal for consumers and mail-center operators. There is no mention of an API reference or runnable examples, and probes for an OpenAPI spec and llms.txt all returned 404.

A SaaS virtual mailbox service could plausibly publish an API spec, so this axis applies. The evidence shows no downloadable OpenAPI or equivalent spec: probes of common OpenAPI/Swagger paths all returned 404, and no first-party docs mention a public API at all.

A virtual mailbox SaaS could plausibly offer a test or sandbox environment for API integrations, so this axis applies. The evidence pack only covers consumer and business mail-handling features. Probes found no llms.txt and no OpenAPI spec, and nothing mentions a sandbox, test mode, or separation from production data.

Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS virtual-mailbox platform, so a versioned public API with a deprecation policy is a fair question for it, but the evidence shows no API at all. The docs cover only app and web-portal mail management, and the probes found no OpenAPI or Swagger spec (all candidate paths 404) and no llms.txt. Nothing mentions API versioning or a deprecation policy.

Bulk actions across many mail items, such as batch scan, forward or shred, are a fair question for a virtual mailbox service, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes per-item actions, like requesting that a single letter be scanned, forwarded or shredded. Nothing documents selecting and acting on many items at once, and the probes found no API (no OpenAPI spec, no llms.txt) through which bulk operations could be scripted.

Automation rules, such as auto-scanning or auto-forwarding mail on arrival, are a fair capability for a virtual mailbox service, so the axis applies. However, the evidence only describes manual, per-item requests: tapping to scan, forward or shred, and scheduling a pickup. Nothing documents user-defined rules or event-triggered automatic actions.

Recurring automation is a fair question for a virtual mailbox service, which could plausibly offer things like scheduled recurring forwarding or automated mail-handling rules, so the axis applies. However, the evidence documents only on-demand requests (scan, forward, shred) and a one-off option to schedule a pickup day and time. That is an adjacent feature, not recurring jobs or workflows. Probes also found no API or OpenAPI spec, and nothing describes a recurring schedule or workflow engine.

A virtual mailbox SaaS could plausibly offer automation rules such as auto-scan or auto-forward, so the axis applies. The evidence shows only manual, per-item requests (scan, forward, shred) through the app or portal. Nothing shows automation rules, version history, review workflows or rollback, and probes found no public API or OpenAPI spec.

Bulk data export is a fair question for a virtual mailbox platform, so the axis applies. The evidence only shows that mail is scanned to PDFs, kept in unlimited online storage, and can be viewed individually. Nothing documents bulk export of scans or mail-history metadata, and no API or OpenAPI spec was found (probes returned 404).

Anytime Mailbox's homepage lists 'Check Deposit' as a feature, but says only 'select locations offer check deposit,' so availability depends on the mail center chosen. Nothing describes how the deposit happens, including endorsement, bank delivery or reconciliation. Missing for 10: universal availability across locations, documented endorsement and deposit workflow, reconciliation or deposit confirmation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

Flagging or prioritizing government and legal mail is a fair axis for a virtual mailbox and mail-center platform. The evidence only shows generic envelope scanning, open/scan requests, forwarding, shredding and multi-user access. Nothing documents detecting, flagging or prioritizing IRS, state, or service-of-process mail, or any deadline alerts.

Anytime Mailbox's own site confirms check deposit exists, but only at select locations, under a bare 'Check Deposit' heading. None of the terms the founder asked about are published in the evidence. missing for 10: list of supported banks, per-deposit fee schedule, deposit turnaround time, disposition of the physical check after deposit (return/shred/store), and any independent corroboration.

The evidence pack shows no entity services from Anytime Mailbox. There is nothing on LLC formation, registered agent service, lease agreements for foreign qualification, or residency-grade addresses. The claim that the address 'meets business registration requirements in most states' describes the core mailbox address itself, not a paired entity service. The 'bundle & save' offer covers mail and calls only.

Anytime Mailbox is a virtual mailbox/CMRA service, so guided USPS Form 1583 completion is a fair question for this product. However, nothing in the evidence pack mentions Form 1583, pre-filled forms, online notarization, or ID requirements. The pack covers only the address, mail scanning, forwarding and team-access features, so the applicable capability is unevidenced.

First-party docs show self-serve forwarding: with a few taps from the phone app or web portal, users can forward letters or packages to a different address, domestically or internationally, without contacting support. Nothing documents the rest of the story. 'Adding an Additional Recipient' (docs-29) covers who can receive mail at the mailbox, not saved forwarding destinations, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: rule-based or automatic forwarding, saved forwarding addresses, carrier/shipping-speed selection, cost shown before confirming, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

The evidence shows only self-service help-center articles and in-app mail action requests (scan, forward, shred), which are adjacent features rather than human support channels. Nothing documents phone, email, or live-agent support for a specific piece of mail, and no response-time expectations are stated. The mail-center logo/contact-info branding note is about operator white-labeling, not a documented support path.

Anytime Mailbox documents a broad location network: 'Choose from 2500+ locations' and 'Find a location near you'. It also supports holding multiple mailboxes in different locations. The note that 'select locations offer check deposit' implies capabilities vary by location, but nothing shows a per-location feature view before signup, and international coverage is not stated. missing for 10: explicit evidence of locations in multiple countries, a documented per-location capability or feature comparison shown before signup, independent or hands-on corroboration.

The evidence has no documentation of facility physical controls, staff background screening, or encryption of scanned mail. The only related wording is passing marketing language: 'securely shred,' 'secure forwarding address,' and 'log in via our secure cloud.' None of these describe how mail is physically secured or how scans are digitally protected, so they don't count as documentation of this capability.

A documented public API for listing mail items and downloading scans is a fair question for a virtual mailbox service, so the axis applies. The evidence only covers manual access through the phone app, web portal and multi-user team sharing, with no developer API documented. The OpenAPI and llms.txt probes all returned 404, which offers no sign of a public API.

Event notifications for new mail or completed scans are a fair question for a virtual mailbox service, but the evidence never mentions webhooks, Zapier triggers or any outbound event mechanism. The docs only cover viewing, scanning, forwarding and shredding mail through the app and web portal. Probes found no public API spec (OpenAPI paths and llms.txt all returned 404).

The evidence documents that mail is scanned to PDFs, uploaded to the account, and kept in free unlimited online storage. Nothing in the pack mentions OCR of scanned contents or searching the archive by sender, content, or date. Scanning and storage are adjacent features, so they earn no credit toward a searchable OCR'd archive.

Anytime Mailbox documents on-request open-and-scan of letter contents delivered as PDFs, going beyond envelope images ("Open and Scan Mail (PDFs)", operator opens and scans contents on request). Nothing states a scan turnaround or that the PDFs are searchable, and scanning is on-request rather than automatic. Missing for 10: stated same/next-business-day turnaround, searchable/OCR PDFs, independent or hands-on corroboration of scan quality and speed.

API parity is a fair question for a SaaS virtual-mailbox platform, but the pack documents only phone-app and web-portal management. Nothing shows a public API, and the probes for an OpenAPI spec and llms.txt all returned 404.

Anytime Mailbox is a SaaS virtual-mailbox and mail-center software platform, and software products like this could publish source under an open license, so the axis applies. The evidence pack contains nothing about source availability, a public repository, or an open license. The only technical-openness probes (llms.txt and OpenAPI) both returned 404 and say nothing about source code.

First-party docs say the address can be used for online shopping, that operators scan packages and labels, and that users can forward letters and packages domestically or internationally or schedule a pickup. Missing for 10: explicit acceptance of all major carriers (UPS/FedEx/DHL/USPS), package consolidation, hands-on or independent confirmation.

Missing for 10: per-plan scan allowances, per-item fees for extra scans, forwarding, physical storage, and check deposit, and a full public plan comparison or pricing table.
